chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from al-Muthanna, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym. He said: I heard a man from the Ansar say:

While the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was sheltering in the shade of a tree on an intensely hot day, a man came and removed his clothes, then began rolling on the scorching ground, burning his back once, his stomach once, and his forehead once, saying: "O self, taste this! For what is with God, Mighty and Majestic, is greater than what you have done to yourself." And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was watching what he was doing.

Then the man put on his clothes and came forward. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) gestured to him with his hand and called him. He said to him: "O servant of God! I saw you do something that I have not seen anyone among the people do. What caused you to do what you did?" The man said: "Fear of God, Mighty and Majestic, caused me to do that. I said to my self: O self, taste this! For what is with God is greater than what you have done to yourself."

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "You have feared your Lord as He is truly to be feared. Indeed, your Lord boasts about you to the people of heaven." Then he said to his companions: "O you who are present, come closer to your companion so that he may pray for you." So they came closer to him and he prayed for them,
saying: "O God, gather our affairs upon guidance, make piety our provision, and Paradise our final abode."

key_terms.الرمضاء: al-Ramda': the scorching ground heated by the sun
key_terms.ليباهي: Yubahi: to boast about, to take pride in someone
key_terms.مخافة: Makhafah: fear, dread, awe of God

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say to the man who rolled on the scorching ground out of fear of God?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Amali of al-Saduq recounts an incident during the Prophet's time in which a man deliberately rolled on scorching hot ground as self-discipline out of fear of God's punishment in the Hereafter. The Prophet (SAWW) commended him, declaring that God boasts about him to the angels, and asked the companions to seek his supplication.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. al-Faddal from al-Muthanna from Layth b. Abi Sulaym. He said: I heard a man from the Ansar say:

We were with the Messenger of Allah (s), shaded by the shade of a tree on an intensely hot day, when a man came, removed [some of] his clothes, and rolled in the scorching heat. He was on his back once, on his stomach once, and on his side once, saying: “O self! Taste this, for what is with Allah is greater than what you have done to yourself!” So, the Messenger of Allah (s) was looking at what he was doing.

Then, the man put on his clothes and came forward. So, the Prophet (s) gestured to him with his hand and called to him. So, he said to him: O servant of Allah! I have seen you do something that I have not seen any one of the people do. So, what caused you to do what you did? So, the man said: My fear of Allah caused me to do this. I said to myself: “O self! Taste this, for what is with Allah is greater than what you have done to yourself!”

So, the Prophet (s) said: You have feared your Lord as He is to be rightly feared. Your Lord is boasting about you to the people of heaven. Then, he said to his companions: O you who are present! Come closer to your companion so that he may pray for you.
So, they came closer to him, and he prayed for them, saying: O Allah! Gather our affairs upon guidance, increase us in God-consciousness and make Paradise our home.
